# Z.ai GLM-Legal Beats Claude Fable 5 and Kimi K3 on Harvey LAB

By

Michal Sutter

-

Add as a preferredsource on Google

Z.ai just released GLM-Legal. GLM-Legal is a legal AI model from Z.ai, built on GLM-5.3-Flash and trained for agentic legal work. It targets contract review, evidence analysis and compliance research. The key result is a 19.2% all-pass rate on Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark (LAB). That is nearly 3x its base model’s 6.7%. For developers, the catch is access: the API is application-only for now.

## TL;DR [...] ## TL;DR

 Size: Built on GLM-5.3-Flash, a 320B-total, 18B-active MoE with a 1M-token context and 128K max output. Z.ai lists no separate GLM-Legal parameter count.
 Runs on: Z.ai’s hosted API only, by application. No public weights. The base model self-hosts on multi-GPU servers via vLLM or SGLang, with FP8 weights.
 Performance: Top-10 on Harvey LAB at a fraction of frontier cost. Within 2.3 points of the LegalBench leader.
 Best: 19.17% Harvey LAB task pass rate, #7 of 79 on Vals AI, at $0.15 per test.
 Worst: 41.83% on Vals AI’s Legal Research Bench, below its own base model (45.19%).
 Bottom line:
  + Best: frontier-class legal agent scores at about 1/128 the cost of Claude Fable 5.
  + Worst: gated beta with no price, no weights and slow runs (1h12m per task). [...] ## What is GLM-Legal?

GLM-Legal is a domain-specialized version of GLM-5.3-Flash for law firms, in-house counsel and compliance teams. The base is Z.ai’s first natively multimodal GLM-5 model. It has 320B total parameters with 18B active. It mixes sparse and linear attention to cut long-context serving cost. It reads text, images, video and files, and outputs text.

## How was GLM-Legal trained?

Training ran in 2 stages:

 Mid-training on expanded legal corpora, to strengthen reasoning from facts to rules to conclusions.
 Post-training with reinforcement learning across tens of thousands of legal task environments.

What it is  
GLM-Legal is a domain-specialized legal model from Z.ai, the Beijing-based lab behind the GLM model family — the same lineage that produced GLM-4, GLM-4.5, and GLM-4.6, releases that have earned Z.ai a reputation as one of the most credible open-weight developers outside the United States. The new model is positioned squarely at legal workflows: contract review and drafting, statutory interpretation, case-law-grounded question answering, and compliance analysis — the document-heavy work that dominates junior lawyer hours and legal operations budgets. [...] Z.ai reports that the model improves over its general-purpose GLM base on legal reasoning and retrieval-oriented evaluations, with particular emphasis on long-context tasks where statutes, precedents, and contract clauses must be cross-referenced across tens of thousands of tokens. Those numbers are vendor-reported for now; independent evaluation will determine whether the gains survive contact with adversarial legal benchmarks. What is not in dispute is the strategy: start from a strong general base, apply intensive domain post-training, and price it in line with the rest of the GLM line — aggressively, with the open-weight posture Z.ai has favored across its recent releases.…  
  
  
  
#AI #LLM #GenAI #MachineLearning #TechNews [...] Z.ai's GLM-Legal Shows Where AI Profit Margins Are Migrating: Verticals  
  
For roughly two years, the default assumption in AI product circles has been that general frontier models would eventually absorb every vertical application. Why fine-tune a legal model when the next GPT-class release passes the bar exam out of the box? Z.ai's announcement of GLM-Legal is the latest, and sharpest, counter-signal: the pendulum is swinging back toward domain specialists — and those specialists may increasingly come from China's open-weight ecosystem rather than Silicon Valley's API oligopoly.

Z.ai released GLM-Legal on October 12, 2026, a legal model built on GLM-5.3-Flash and trained for contract review, evidence analysis and compliance work. Its launch post at 16:10 UTC says it “matches frontier models on mainstream legal benchmarks”, and its tech blog puts the headline number at a 19.2% all-pass rate on Harvey’s Legal Agent Benchmark (LAB). Access is by application for now: “Apply for API access”, with Z.ai’s AutoClaw desktop agent to follow.

We checked the number against the independent leaderboard. It holds, and it tells a more useful story than Z.ai’s chart does.
